主要内容: Chesapeake Energy Corporation (NASDAQ: CHK) successfully emerged from Chapter 11 financial restructuring on February 9, 2021. The company's debt balance decreased significantly, from $9,095 million as of June 30, 2020, to $1,271 million. It issued $1 billion in senior unsecured notes at an average coupon under 5.7%, and entered into a credit line with a $2.5 billion borrowing base, including a $221 million non-revolving loan facility and a $1,750 million revolving loan facility. The company projected its full-year 2021 average daily production to be approximately 427,000 barrels of oil equivalent (boe), with planned capital expenditures of around $700 million. A new Board of Directors was appointed, including an Environmental and Social Governance Committee. Approximately $7.8 billion in debt was converted to equity, with new common shares (ticker: CHK) and warrants (CHKEW, CHKEZ, CHKEL) to be listed on NASDAQ. The company’s balance sheet and cost structure have been improved, positioning it for sustainable free cash flow and environmental excellence.
